teaser: A founder's exit is the day someone else buys control, which can come long before the shares go. Leave then, and agree the terms at the start.
core_idea: A founder's exit is the sale of control, not of the last share; control can pass to boards and investor vetoes while the founder still owns a majority, and that is the moment to leave, on terms negotiated at the start, as Mourinho's priced exits show, with a number written down early to recognise when enough is enough.

nodes.label: Ownership is not control
nodes.summary: Boards, vetoes, drag-along; or dual-class votes.

nodes.label: Rich versus king
nodes.summary: Half no longer CEO by year three.

quotes.text: The exit is when somebody buys control.
So the exit is not the day you sell your last share. It is the day you are no longer the one deciding.
